summary: LAN hotplug causes split-tunnel route removal and DNS search-suffix loss — internal service failures
description: Issue summary: After docking/undocking or plugging an ethernet cable while connected to corporate Wi‑Fi, some Windows laptops lose the VPN split-tunnel routes and the corporate DNS search suffix for the active interface. Impact: Users cannot resolve internal hostnames (e.g., console.redwood.local) and cannot reach internal services despite the VPN status showing 'connected'. Environment: Multiple Surface and MacBook devices observed but reproduces reliably on Windows 11 corporate image with Agent v2.14. Observed behavior: - VPN connection remains connected but traffic to internal subnets is routed to the LAN interface and then dropped. - DNS queries for short names stop appending the corporate search suffix, causing NXDOMAIN for internal names. - Reconnecting VPN or toggling Wi‑Fi does not restore routes until user reboots or runs manual interface reset commands. This blocks internal console access and developer workflows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Boot Windows 11 corporate laptop and connect to office Wi‑Fi (corp-wifi).
2) Establish WireGuard-based VPN via corporate client (Agent v2.14).
3) Plug in docking station or direct ethernet cable (hotplug) which brings up the wired interface with lower metric.
4) Observe that VPN shows connected in client UI, but internal hostnames (short names) no longer resolve and services on 10.40.0.0/16 are unreachable.
5) Run 'ipconfig /all' and 'route print' to inspect missing split-tunnel routes and missing DNS search suffix on the active interface.
logs: WireGuard client log excerpt (2026-03-12T10:14:02Z): peer=10.8.0.1 handshake ok; added routes: 10.40.0.0/16 -> wg0
Windows System event (2026-03-12T10:15:05Z): Network profile changed. Interface ethernet0 metric set to 10.
Subsequent WireGuard log (2026-03-12T10:15:07Z): routes flushed for interface change; no re-add of split routes due to client error 'IF_STATE_MISMATCH'
DnsClient service (2026-03-12T10:15:09Z): DNS search list cleared for interface ethernet0
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Client is not re-applying split-tunnel routes and DNS suffix on interface change; likely race between Windows network binding change and our agent's interface watcher.
Packet capture on affected host shows internal DNS queries sent to gateway DNS (192.168.1.1) after hotplug; WireGuard encapsulation still present for other traffic but no specific 10.40 routes.
Reproduced on Windows 11 with fast-APM networking driver; could not reproduce on macOS Catalina test node (suggests Windows-specific client/OS interaction).
SRE ran live debug: triggered hotplug while tailing agent logs; agent logged 'interface_added' then 'interface_removed' rapidly and skipped route re-apply due to debounce logic set to 8s.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-12): User reported this after docking at SF office. Affected services: console, internal artifact registry. Several devs blocked.
Diego Ramirez (2026-03-12): Assigned for triage. Asked for ipconfig/route print and agent logs. Requested user to avoid reboot for now to capture traces.
SRE-oncall (2026-03-12): Captured pcap and logs. Confirmed DNS queries going to local AP and not our resolver. WireGuard remains up but split routes absent.
Client-Eng (2026-03-13): Noted debounce logic introduced in Agent v2.14 to avoid flapping; suspect it suppresses re-apply on quick interface state changes. Preparing patch branch.

Diego Ramirez (2026-03-13): Workaround provided to users: run 'netsh interface set interface "Wi-Fi" metric=1' and then 'wg-quick down wg0 && wg-quick up wg0' or reboot. Added temporary Powershell script to fix suffix and routes.
Client-Eng (2026-03-14): Created PR #1218 to reduce debounce window and add explicit re-apply on interface metric change. Linked PR below.
resolution: Mitigation: Published a temporary PowerShell fix script in #internal-support slack and deployed Agent v2.14.1 to staging with reduced debounce time and extra check to re-apply split routes when a new interface appears with a lower metric. Permanent fix: Client-Eng to merge PR #1218 and add test automation for interface hotplug scenarios. Rollout plan: staged rollout to 10% of Windows corp fleet by 2026-03-16, monitor DNS resolution metrics and internal access error rates. Follow-up action: update runbook to include the quick-fix commands and add an automated endpoint remediation script in the Console.
